relevance_note: The paper describes four in-scope patients with succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency and ALDH5A1 variants, each with individual-level detail ("Patient 1 was a 3-year-old female"), plus relatives tested for the same variants.
method_note: Read only the paper Markdown, schema_ssadh_v5.json and extraction_rules_v1.md. No script was used; both tables were transcribed by hand and re-checked cell by cell against the Markdown. The Markdown mixes ordinary spaces with thin spaces (U+2009) inside variant strings ('c.527G > A', 'c.800 T > G', 'c.1344-2delA/c.1529C > T') and between numbers and units ('86 days', '5 days', '3 days', '2-4 Hz', '23 days', '8 m', '< 0.001'); these are reproduced with \u2009 escapes, while Table 1 and Table 2 pipe spacing uses ordinary spaces. Stacked cells (v6, D-31): no cell in this paper contains ' / ' stacked values; Table 1 holds one value per patient column and Table 2 one value per 'Case' column, so no positional reading of stacked cells was needed. Table 2 column headers are 'Case1', 'Case2', 'Case 3', 'Case 4', read as patients 1-4 in the same order as Table 1 ('| Patients | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |'); that column-to-patient mapping is positional and is used only for the urine organic acid values. Table 1's legend ('F female, M male, y years, d days, m months, N no, Y yes, UN unknown') defines N as no, so N cells were used as 'excluded' with the legend as a second span; 'UN' (unknown) and empty cells were 'not reported'. Contradictions and uncertainties: (1) patient 3 - Table 1 'Sleep disturbances' = N but the text says he was admitted 'due to developmental delay complicated with lack of sleep'; both phenotypic rows are emitted and the checklist item is 'not reported'. (2) The abstract says 'these four mutations have been described previously' but also calls c.800 T > G 'a novel discovery', and says 'mutations at five sites' while the conclusion says 'five ALDH5A1 gene mutations' in four patients; I recorded five distinct variant descriptions (eleven person-variant rows). (3) The Discussion sentence 'Patient 2 and 4 exhibited decreased attention and sleep disturbances, respectively' pairs the two features one way while Table 1 marks 'Sleep disturbances' Y for both patients 2 and 4; for patient 2's sleep disturbance I used the Table 1 cell only, for patient 4 both. (4) Patient 2 has 'poor head control' in the text while Table 1 marks 'Hypotonia' N; poor head control is not stated to be hypotonia, so hypotonia stays excluded and 'poor head control' is recorded separately as a motor finding (I mapped it to the checklist item 'gross or fine motor deficits' as observed). (5) Patient 1: 'She had no movement or language disorders during the postictal period' versus 'language delay'; the first statement is limited to the postictal period, so it is recorded as its own excluded row and the language delay as observed, and the checklist item 'speech or language impairment' is observed. Variant fields: the parts printed in one parenthesis, 'c.527G > A/c.691G > A (p.G176E/p.E231K)', were paired by printed order (cDNA1-protein1, cDNA2-protein2). No transcript is attached to any variant (the only accession printed, NM_170740, is in the methods), so transcript_as_stated is 'not reported' everywhere; no genomic description is printed. Variant type is stated only for c.1344-2delA ('located in the intron splice site' -> splice). Zygosity comes from each patient's own sentence; zygosity of carrier parents is 'not reported' because the paper never states it. In-silico predictions and conservation are recorded in functional_evidence_statement (no functional assay is reported); for patient 1 the two Polyphen2 predictions are printed as a pair without saying which variant is which, so they are not reported for either of her variants. Relatives: mother/father of patient 1 and mother/father of patient 2 are described with the variant they carry (the mother of patient 2 carries c.1529C > T; the healthy father does not carry it and gets no variant row); the two parents of patient 3 get variant rows for c.800 T > G because the paper says he inherited it from them; the two parents of patient 4 get no variant row because the paper says only that the two mutations were 'separately inherited from both of her parents' without saying which parent carries which. The mother of patient 2 is also described as having 'an abnormal reproductive history', with a first baby who 'died of convulsion at 23 days after birth'; that baby is recorded as 'sibling of Patient 2' (a relative described in relation to an in-scope person), while the ectopic second pregnancy is not a person and gets no row. Group and disease-level statements (for example 'Hypotonia and neuropsychiatric problems each have occurred in 70% of patients'), study criteria and the 100 healthy controls were not used as person-level evidence; the controls are not counted in cohort_size_as_stated (4 patients). 'We have previously reported these two mutations [8, 12]' concerns the variants, not the patients, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is false. No treatment is named for any patient, so treatment_summary is 'not reported' everywhere ('died of pneumonia despite rescue efforts' was not read as a treatment).
